label: Body plans
description: The unit's upper-body shape and silhouette (legs and wheels live in mobility, scale in size). Each body lists the mobility types and sizes it fits and how its weapons can be mounted. A transforming unit records its second form's body in its modes. A mode records a second body only when the upper body changes shape (a mech folding into a jet); bracing, deploying or raising a gun in place keeps the body.

terms.label: Humanoid
terms.description: A soldier or hero on two feet.

terms.label: Power suit
terms.description: Powered armour, an exosuit or a battlesuit around one pilot. At small size (one soldier's size, such as power armour) it is infantry; at medium size or bigger it is a walker.

terms.label: Creature
terms.description: A war animal or creature of any size, from an attack dog to a giant beast.

terms.label: Hull with turret
terms.description: A chassis with a rotating turret: the classic tank shape, also on legs.

terms.label: Fixed-gun hull
terms.description: A chassis with a forward-fixed main gun and no main turret, like a tank destroyer.

terms.label: Open mount
terms.description: An open-topped vehicle with an exposed weapon mount and crew, like a gun truck or buggy.

terms.label: Troop carrier
terms.description: An enclosed hull with a passenger compartment, with at most a small turret or a remote weapon mount: APC or IFV.

terms.label: Multi-turret giant
terms.description: A very large chassis with two or more independently turning turrets, like a super-heavy tank.

terms.label: Humanoid mech
terms.description: A two-legged mech with a torso and arms.

terms.label: Reverse-joint walker
terms.description: A cockpit or gun pod on backward-bending legs.

terms.label: Spider frame
terms.description: A body slung between several visible legs, from a tiny robot to a giant walker.

terms.label: Gas envelope
terms.description: An airship or blimp with a gondola.

terms.label: Micro-bot
terms.description: A compact robot on wheels, tracks, a hover pad or rotors, with no prominent legs.

terms.label: Launcher rack
terms.description: A light chassis carrying an exposed launcher rack, radar mast or mortar: mobile anti-air, rocket artillery, sensor carriers.

tie_breaks.rule: A hull whose riders sit hidden and protected inside is box-carrier, even with a small turret or a roof launcher (most APCs and IFVs). Hull-turret is for tanks, whose turret and gun are the main body. Open-mount needs crew or riders who sit exposed. Launcher-rack is for a vehicle built around an exposed rack, mast or mortar, with no passenger compartment.

Power suit when the sources say the soldier wears powered armour, an exosuit or a battlesuit (Space Marines, the PlanetSide 2 MAX, Elementals). Humanoid for a soldier in ordinary body armour or carapace, however heavy. Size and armour class follow their own rules: one soldier's size is small, and the armour class comes from the armour-class steps and the soldier rule.

Decide by where the main gun sits: fixed in the hull is casemate, even when a small turret on top carries another seat's gun (the Magrider); in a turret is hull-turret. A roof turret's free aim then breaks casemate's mount rule, and the validator lists that as atypical.
